title: QBench weekly retrospective — quant & eval ops
body:
Week covered: 2027-06-14 -> 2027-06-20
Attendees: Asha, Marco, Jordan, Priya, Evan (plus async notes from Sasha)

Purpose: short retrospective for QBench experiments this week — track quantization experiments, eval regressions, and progress on onboarding new model variants into the catalog. Capture decisions, blockers, and action items.

SUMMARY (TL;DR):
- Two promising PTQ flows: AWQ-4 (fast path) and mixed-int8/4 fallback. AWQ-4 gives ~1.8–2.0x throughput vs baseline float on 40GB A100 under our microbatching profile with an average eval drop of ~6% absolute on selected instruction tasks.
- GPTQ-4 variant still unstable on long-context evals (ppl/spike beyond token 2048), flagged as DO NOT ROLL for now.
- KV-cache microbatching + prefix-cache reuse improved p95 latency by ~12% on rw-13b-ptq tests.
- Onboarding: rw-33b-ptq candidate build is ready; canary schedule proposed for Dedicated pool on 2027-06-28.
- Major blocker: reproducibility of AWQ quant seeds across CUDA drivers (CUDA 12.3 vs 12.1 discrepancy).

EXPERIMENT NOTES (detailed):
1) AWQ-4 path (engine: qbench-v2, hw: A100-40GB)
   - Config: per-channel block size=128, outlier threshold=2.5, activation clipping=none.
   - Perf: 1.9x throughput (tokens/s) vs baseline float vRAM profile reduced ~38%.
   - Eval: instruction-following subset (internal: redwood-instr-2027-05, ~3.2k prompts): avg exact-match delta -6.1 pts, F1 drop concentrated on multi-step reasoning prompts.
   - Notes: acceptable for non-critical low-SLA routes; suggest experiments with small activation clipping to reduce reasoning drop.

2) GPTQ-4 path (engine: gptq-runner)
   - Config: quantize layers 1..L-3, group size=32.
   - Perf: 2.1x throughput observed on short-context tests.
   - Failure: on long-context (>=2048 tokens) observed perplexity spikes and repeated token loops on ~12% of prompts.
   - Decision: flag GPTQ-4 as DO NOT ROLL until root cause addressed.

3) Mixed int8/4 fallback (hybrid execution)
   - Approach: hot layers in int8, attention/MLP tail in 4-bit AWQ.
   - Perf: 1.6x throughput, eval delta -3.5 pts on instruction set, p95 latency slightly worse than pure AWQ due to inter-op overhead but stable.
   - Action: optimize kernel fusion to reduce inter-op overhead (see ENG-4721).

4) KV-cache + microbatching tests
   - Setup: microbatch sizes tuned from 1->8, prefix cache reuse across requests with identical prefixes for sessioned traffic.
   - Results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved by 12%, memory tail reduced by ~18% (GC and eviction frequency down).
   - Observed regression: for very small prompts (<16 tokens), batching increases median latency for single-request routing; route policy should avoid batching on low-token singletons.

EVALS AND METRICS
- Datasets used: redwood-instr-2027-05 (3.2k prompts), rw-eval-longform-1k, custom-cs-synth-800.
- Key metrics recorded in QBench dashboard: perplexity, exact-match, F1, hallucination-rate (heuristic), token-efficiency (tokens per correct answer).
- Example numbers (rw-13b-ptq on A100): baseline float p99 latency 540ms, AWQ-4 p99 460ms; throughput baseline 70 t/s, AWQ-4 130 t/s.
- Regression alerts: one eval run on 2027-06-19 crossed our 5% EM drop threshold for rw-33b-ptq candidate — investigation shows distribution shift in prompt sampling (longer multi-turn examples introduced).

ONBOARDING STATUS: rw-33b-ptq
- Build: artifact rw-33b-ptq-v0.3 created and uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-models/rw-33b-ptq/v0.3).
- Canary plan: Dedicated pool subset 4, start 2027-06-28, 24h canary -> roll to full pool if no regressions.
- Pre-canary checks: eval suite passrate >= 94% on redwood-instr-2027-05, perf target >=1.5x throughput vs float under standard batch. Current pass rate 92.4% (needs one more iteration).

BLOCKERS / RISKS
- CUDA driver inconsistency: AWQ results vary between CUDA 12.1 and 12.3 (repro seed drift). Priority: HIGH. Owner: Marco. Ticket: ML-1583.
- Eval drift from new prompt sets causing false positives for regressions. Short-term mitigation: add stratified sampling and label groups in eval runner. Owner: Jordan.
- Kernel fusion work needed to reduce mixed-int8/4 overhead — risk to latency SLOs if left as-is. Owner: Priya.

DECISIONS MADE THIS WEEK
- Hold GPTQ-4 rollouts until long-context instability root cause identified.
- Proceed with rw-33b-ptq canary but gate on tightened eval pass criteria (added longform sampling to canary suite).
- Default route policy update: prefer prefix-cache-enabled workers for sessioned traffic; exclude microbatching for single-token short prompts.

ACTION ITEMS (owners + ETA):
- Marco: reproduce AWQ seed discrepancy across CUDA versions and add deterministic seed wrapper in quant-tooling. ETA: 2027-06-25. (ML-1583)
- Jordan: add stratified sampling to eval runner + create a small longform holdout set for canaries. ETA: 2027-06-24. (ENG-4721)
- Priya: prototype kernel-fusion patch for mixed-int8/4 path (follow up PR: quant-bench#234). ETA: 2027-06-30.
- Evan: prepare canary run checklist and automated rollback hook for Dedicated pool (playbook link added to Confluence). ETA: 2027-06-26.
- Asha: run one more AWQ-4 activation clipping sweep (clip=0.1,0.2,0.3) to see if reasoning drop reduces without performance loss. ETA: 2027-06-24.

OPEN QUESTIONS / THINKING OUT LOUD
- Is activation clipping the right long-term fix for AWQ reasoning drop or is layer-wise re-quantization needed?
- For mixed int8/4, how much latency overhead is acceptable before we declare the hybrid approach too risky for paid-hosted routes?
- Should we add a "long-context stress" job to the nightly regression suite that runs on a smaller subset but covers >10k tokens sessions?

NOTES TO SELF / SCRATCHES
- Quick experiment snippet: run qbench-local --model rw-33b-ptq-v0.3 --batch 2 --microbatch 4 --profile > /tmp/qb-20270621.log
- Slack refs: #qbench (thread pinned: "awq-vs-gptq-6-2027"), PR: quant-bench#234 for kernel fusion work.

MEETING FOLLOW-UPS (next meeting: 2027-06-28 10:00 PT)
- Check Marco progress on ML-1583 and Jordan on strat-sampling.
- Post-canary review (if rw-33b-ptq goes live) to capture real-traffic diffs.
- Sync with SRE on Dedicated pool autoscaler thresholds for canaries.

ATTACHMENTS / ARTIFACTS (in-drive):
- qbench-run-2027-06-18.csv (perf dump)
- eval-report-rw-33b-ptq-v0.3.pdf (quick view)

END.
